changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For subscription and membership businesses, especially regional ones, open with involuntary churn instead of global infrastructure: "Some of your churn is members who never meant to leave: their card failed, they didn't cancel. We get them back." Keep M1 for buyers who actually operate across many countries and currencies.
changes.why: The global opener drew silence from a US-and-Canada studio chain, while the buying trigger was board-reported churn split into real cancellations and failed cards, which the customer described as "members who never meant to leave."

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For membership and subscription prospects, use M10 as a proof offer before the proposal: "Send us one month of your failed renewals and we'll show you which members come back." Make it a standard pre-proposal step, and put the result in front of whoever signs.
changes.why: Failed-payment recovery was what got a reaction, and the deal turned only when the solutions engineer ran the customer's own month of failed renewals ("Their file, not our average"); the silent controller asked for that spreadsheet and signed four days later.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: Stop leading with unified commerce for customers who run their front desks through vertical software (for example, studio management systems) unless we can demo our reader working inside their own front-desk software. Until then, use their words, "front desk" and "readers", and name the partner integration and its status explicitly. Do not say the line between online and in-store "has disappeared".
changes.why: The customer heard unified commerce as "is that the readers?", which shifted the conversation to hardware where the incumbent was embedded; we couldn't show the reader inside their studio software, studio managers would "revolt" without that, and the studios stayed with Global Payments pending the partner piece.

changes.change: Add a finance-facing one-pager for the controller or CFO, ready before the contract reaches them: the cost of members lost to failed cards, using the customer's own data, plus plain answers on contract term, termination fees and what it costs to switch.
changes.why: The controller held the signature and left the paper sitting for two weeks; his only questions before the data session were about contract term and exit cost, and no part of our pitch was aimed at him.
